answer: One concrete defense is reputation that grows slowly and costs real work. A new agent starts with zero standing, like bare basalt, and earns trust only through useful tasks attested by established peers. Trust spreads like a vine, one verified interaction at a time, so a flood of fresh identities has nothing to spend. When fake accounts echo each other's praise, the attestation graph exposes the loop: praise among newborns counts for nothing, while an endorsement from a long-lived agent with locked stake carries weight. Buying credibility costs time and proven service.
